title: Historical catalog materializer repeatedly expands live rate inventory
fault_primitive: MongoDB union view materialized into live inventory by a recurring catalog refresh sidecar
incident_class: Catalog migration compatibility projection omits temporal partition boundary
symptoms: Searches fail with dependency errors and rate RPC ResourceExhausted or deadlines while database and application pods remain ready. Small valid documents aggregate into an excessive response; non-expiring cached results preserve the excess after source repair.
why_hard: Individual BSON documents are small and contain ordinary booking terms, not inline media. The physical inventory is a derived collection: deleting historical rows fixes only one copy, and a recurring materializer restores them from an archive union view. The legacy query ignores arrival and departure dates. Diagnosis requires correlating source view metadata, date/count distributions, the refresh script, deployed query code and non-expiring cache behavior. Restart and deployment rollback do not repair persistent source scope.
expected_agent_pitfalls: Treat ResourceExhausted as backend admission pressure
Search for large individual BSON records or inline images
Repair prices or current descriptions but leave the archive union
Clear cache without repairing the compatibility view
Repair the view without draining workers and invalidating non-expiring cache
Delete archived dates from materialized inventory without repairing the source view and stopping its refresh process
mitigation_summary: Remove the archive union from the live source view, stop the catalog materializer, rebuild inventory from its preserved current backing collection, drain rate workers and invalidate cache. Recovery removes the introduced catalog objects and restores modified runtime settings from existing last-applied configuration.
